dropReason: Confirmed against AoN equipment-2376 (Treasure Vault Remastered pg. 190) and equipment-4905 (legacy). The printed text is a trap, not a bonus: 'while you remain loyal to another deity, you believe the cassock grants you a +2 item bonus to Religion checks and a +1 item bonus to the divine skill of the deity to whom you believe the cassock is dedicated. It does neither. The GM secretly adjusts your checks with those skills.' The bonuses function only if the wearer converts to the cassock's TRUE unholy deity, which is GM-secret and unmodelled by the app, so the condition can never resolve true on a sheet. Authoring it would put a star promising +2 Religion on a character who has no bonus at all. The entry also omitted the negation clause ('If you have multiple equal or lower item bonuses to the affected skills, the cassock takes precedence, negating those bonuses'), which is the only real mechanical effect and is a SUPPRESSION, not a bonus — a situational star cannot express it. corruption-cassock is priced (1150 gp) and ownable, so this is a rules defect, not an ownability one: no situational entry belongs on it in any form.
